title: Negative possession with singular owners
summary: Build singular-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
objectives: Build singular-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build singular-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
Choose minulla, sinulla, and hänellä. Keep ei and ole together after the owner, then use the complete partitive noun shown or learned.
keyPoints: Build singular-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.

examples.english: I do not have a car.
steps: Begin with the owner minulla. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive autoa (“a car”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a ball.
steps: Begin with the owner sinulla. sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive palloa (“a ball”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: She does not have a pen.
steps: Begin with the owner hänellä. hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kynää (“a pen”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: I do not have a game.
steps: Begin with the owner minulla. minulla means “I as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive peliä (“a game”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a book.
steps: sinulla identifies the singular owner in this negative possession with singular owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
kirjaa (“a book”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kirja + -a.

examples.english: He or she does not have a dog.
steps: hänellä identifies the singular owner in this negative possession with singular owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
koiraa (“a dog”) is the complete regular singular partitive: koira + -a.

examples.english: I do not have a pillow.
steps: minulla identifies the singular owner in this negative possession with singular owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
tyynyä (“a pillow”) is the complete regular singular partitive: tyyny + -ä.

commonMistakes: Keep the requested order: owner + ei ole + partitive noun. Do not leave out ole.
Retain the noun ending when assembling the full sentence: Minulla ei ole koiraa, rather than Minulla ei ole koira.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “I do not have a pen.” Start with the owner. Use minulla (“I as the owner”) and kynää (“a pen”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun.
requiredSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession

sentenceExplanation.translation: I do not have a pen.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with minulla, sinulla and hänellä; do not change it to en or et.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
kynä + -ä = kynää. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Translate “Sinulla ei ole kissaa.” into English. Address one person.
acceptedAnswers: You do not have a cat.
You do not have the cat.
practiceExercises.explanation: Sinulla names one listener as owner; ei ole denies possession, and kissaa is the negative noun form.
